description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements. You may return the answer in any order. It is guaranteed that the answer is unique.
examples:
Input: nums = [1,1,1,2,2,3], k = 2
Output: [1, 2]
Explanation: 1 appears 3 times and 2 appears 2 times.
intuition: After counting frequencies, you need the top k. Sorting frequencies costs O(n log n), but notice that frequencies range from 1 to n. You can create an array of "buckets" where bucket i holds all numbers that appeared exactly i times. Then just walk backwards from the highest bucket to grab the most frequent elements. This is bucket sort applied to frequencies.
approach: Use bucket sort: count frequencies, then create an array of buckets where index i holds all elements that appear i times. Iterate from the highest bucket downward to collect the top k elements. This runs in O(n) time.
jsWalkthrough:
nums = [1,1,1,2,2,3], k = 2

Step 1 — count frequencies:
  count = {1:3, 2:2, 3:1}

Step 2 — fill buckets (index = frequency):
  buckets[1] = [3]     (3 appeared 1 time)
  buckets[2] = [2]     (2 appeared 2 times)
  buckets[3] = [1]     (1 appeared 3 times)

Step 3 — walk backwards from highest:
  freq=6: empty
  freq=5: empty
  freq=4: empty
  freq=3: push 1 → result=[1]
  freq=2: push 2 → result=[1,2] → length===k, return!

return [1, 2]
explanation:
1. Count the frequency of each element using Counter.
2. Create buckets of size (n+1). Index i of this array stores all numbers whose frequency is exactly i.
3. The maximum possible frequency is n (all elements the same), so the array is big enough.
4. Walk backwards from the highest frequency bucket, collecting elements until we have k results.
5. This avoids sorting and runs in O(n) time.
hints: First, count the frequency of each number. Then you need the top k by frequency.
A heap gives O(n log k). Can you do O(n)?
Bucket sort by frequency: the maximum frequency is n, so create n+1 buckets and iterate from the top.

timeComplexityBreakdown.variables: n = numbers; U = distinct values; k = requested results. k ≤ U ≤ n.

phases.label: Scan buckets and collect k results

timeComplexityBreakdown.note: Each distinct value belongs to one bucket. The inner bucket loop does not scan all U values for every frequency.
